1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ( PFA Act), wherein it is alleged that the accused persons had sold misbranded food in violation of Section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 32 (a)(b)(c)
(e) and partial violation of Rule 32(f) and violation of Rule 32(i) and 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules, 1955 punishable under section 16(1) DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another (a) of PFA Act.
2.

M.S. Vats reached at the premises of M/s Bengali Sweet House, 27-34, Bengali Market, New Delhi-110001.
The accused Kishan Dutt Sharma was found Da vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & Another on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52493213/

sentences.text: 1 vending the business of various food articles, including Mogra Namkin which were found stored for sale of human consumption , lying in sealed packets of 200 gms, each bearing identical label declaration.
The food officials lifted the sample of the said food article consisting of 6 sealed packets of Mogra Namkin ready for sale.
It was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed.
Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt and panchanama.
Price of the sample was paid to the vendor.
One counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst(PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA.

Vide report date 30.04.2008, the PA reported that the article was conforming to the standards, yet the sample was found misbranded being in violation of Rule 32 a,b,c,e, partial violation of Rule 32f and violation of Rule 32(i) and 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules.
Based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector as per the instructions of the SDM/LHA.
It was found that Accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma was the vendor of M/s Bengali Sweet House, 27-34, Bengali Market, New Delhi-110001 at the time of taking samples.

Accused No. 2 M/s Bengali Sweet House was a partnership firm DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another and it had appointed accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma as its Nominee under the provisions of PFA Act and Rules and he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said firm being a partnership firm Accused No. 1 Bengali Sweet House was also liable.
The sampled article of food "Mogra Namkin" was manufactured by the firm/accused No. 2 M/s. Bengali Sweet House itself.

After obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA, the present complaint came to be filed against the accused for violation of the section 2(ix)(k) read with Rule 32 (a)(b)(c)(e), partial violation of Rule 32(f) and violation of Rule 32(i) and 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules,
1955 as punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for selling misbranded food.
3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 30.09.2010.

Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation u/s 251 Cr.PC was framed vide order dated 15.04.2011 against the accused persons for commission of offence under Section 7/16 (1)(a) of PFA Act for violation of provisions of Section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act,1954 along with Rule 32 and 36 of PFA Rules,
1955.
4.

At the trial, the prosecution examined four witnesses in support of its case, PW-1 FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta, PW3 Sh. M.S.Vats SDM/LHA and PW4 Sh. Ashok Kumar was part of the team that had visited the premises of accused persons and lifted the sample of Mogra Namkin lying in sealed packets of 200 gms each.
PW2 FI N.N. Sharma also IO in the present case.

These witnesses deposed about the sample proceedings conducted by DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another them on 04.04.2008 and narrated the steps undertaken by them, including disclosing their identity, lifting 6 sealed packets of 200 gms each, dividing the same in three counterparts by considering one sealed packets as one counterpart and separately packing them.

After which complaint Ex.PW2/B was filed before this Court and intimation letter Ex.PW2/C alongwith postal receipts Ex.PW2/D was sent to the accused persons.
These witnesses were cross-examined by Ld. Counsels for accused persons.
5. PW1 denied the suggestion that he did not make any effort to join any public witness.
He also denied the suggestion that the 6 packets of Mogra Namkin which he took as sample were not yet ready for sale.

PW1 also added that he did not inquire from the Department regarding the first violation by the Firm as the policy of issuing warning of first violation under Rule 32 of PFA Rules had been already withdrawn on the date of sample proceedings.

PW3 admitted during his cross-examination that the sample was lifted to analyse the same for adulteration and added that whenever a sample was sent for analysis, it was also ascertained if the sample complied with PFA Rules and was misbranded or not.
He also stated that the packets were suitable containers and admitted that the contents on the same were not complete and therefore was in violation of PFA Rules.
He admitted that removable stickers bearing such information was in violation of Rules.
6. Statement of the accused persons were recorded under section 313 Cr.PC on 25.04.2017 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
Accused No. 1 admitted the sample proceedings.
Accused No. 1 and 2 opted to lead Defence DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another evidence.

sentences.text: 7. Accused No.1 Kishan Dutt Sharma examined himself as DW1 and stated that he was working as a Nominee with M/s. Bengali Sweet House, Bengali Market, New Delhi and on 04.04.2008 a raiding party consisting of three persons including SDM, FA Ashok Kumar and FI Suniti Kumar came at the shop and showed their intention to purchase the sample and FI Suniti Kumar took 6 packets of 200 gm each of Mogra Namkin as a sample and he added that FI did not accept any request and forcibly took the sample and made three counterparts of two packets each and further added that the sample of Mogra Namkin was however declared as per standard.
During his cross-examination by Ld. SPP for complainant, he did not make any complaint in the PFA Department regarding this fact.

8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as both the witnesses have supported its case and there is no contradiction in their testimony.

It is submitted that the accused Da vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & Another on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52493213/
3 persons have failed to rebut the findings as given in the PA Report.

sentences.text:
9. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused No.1 and 2 have argued that accused No.
1 and 2 were falsely implicated and that the sticker on the sample food article was yet to be affixed.
He has also argued that Accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma had no role in the present case.
DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another 10.
I have heard the arguments advanced by Ld. SPP for the complaint and Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused and have carefully perused the material available on record.
11. In a criminal trial, the burden is on the complainant / prosecution to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and has to be necessarily discharged by the prosecution itself by leading cogent and trustworthy evidence.
12. In the present case, there is no serious dispute as to the steps undertaken by PWs in lifting the sample.
All the PWs, who were a part of the team that had lifted the sample, have deposed in corroboration of each other.
No material contradiction can be seen in their testimony that could go to the root of the matter so as to disbelieve them.
They have deposed about steps undertaken by them during sample proceedings and have deposed about compliance of rules while lifting the sample.
No question was put to them regarding non-compliance of any mandatory rule, except putting some general bald suggestions.
The witnesses have also deposed that attempt was made to join public persons as witnesses but none had joined.
There is nothing to disbelieve them or to shake their credibility.
13. The fate of the case depends on quality of witnesses and not their quantity or designation or professions.
There is no rule of law that requires the evidence of food officials to be viewed with any suspicion.
What is required is that attempt is made to join public persons as witnesses as a matter of prudence.

The court DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another is not oblivious of reluctance of public persons to join such legal proceedings that involves lengthy procedural formalities and strict future commitments.

entities.text: court DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But non joining of such witnesses would not negate the testimony of official witnesses when they are otherwise truthful and credit worthy and have withstood the test of cross-examination.
No motive has shown to exist giving them reason to depose falsely against the accused.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed, is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies.
No such inconsistency can be seen in this case.
No violation of any rule or provision has been pointed out by the defence.

14. In the present case charges were framed against accused persons for violation of provisions of section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act, 1954 and for violation of provisions as stated in Rule 32 and 36 of PFA Rules, 1954 punishable U/s. 16(1)(a) r/w Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954.

15. Perusal of the form VI Ex.PW1/B shows that the label has been reproduced wherein it is stated that there was a sticker that mentioned the weight as 200 gm, Bengali Sweet House, price as Rs.28/-
and April'2008.
This document further categorically mentions that there is no other declaration on the packet.

The PA report Ex.PW1/G states that size of label was only 0.9% of the size of packet without declaration of name of commodity DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another ingredients,
complete address, batch number and that the date mentioned was without any reference to packing or manufacturing or best before.

Therefore, the defence of the accused that the sticker was about to be fixed on the sampled food article is not tenable as it has been proved that there was a sticker attached in the sealed packet of sampled food article.

With regard to the role of Accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma, it is seen that it has been stated at Ex.PW1/K-1 that when Albert James Dass would not be present, then Kishan Dutt Sharma would be the alternate nominee and shall be responsible during the time of his duties.

Further, Ex.PW1/L which is letter dated 03.03.2009 issued by M/s. Bengali Sweet House to Food Inspector wherein it has been further clarified that their firm did not dissolve due to the death of one of the partner Sh. Rohtash Chand and continued to be working.

It was also further clarified vide the aforesaid letter that accused Kishan Dutt Sharma continued to be the nominee of their firm despite the death of one of the partner and his continuation was with his consent.
Even the complainant in the present case has mentioned that accused Kishan Dutt Sharma was found vending the sampled article at the time of sampling.
Merely putting suggestions during cross-examination of witness is not sufficient to contradict the evidence that has been led in this behalf conclusively by the complainant.

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid facts and discussions, it has been conclusively proved that the accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma was found vending the sampled food item at the time of sampling and was also the appointed Nominee on behalf of M/s. Bengali Sweet House.

16. With respect to the charges framed against the accused persons, DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma &
another it is seen that perusal of Ex.PW1/B which Notice under Form VI and Ex.PW1/G which is the PA report and other documents on record, it is seen that only the weight, name of M/s. Bengali Sweet House, price and month and year have been provided.

sentences.text: No other information has been provided in the label/sticker.
17. At this stage, it is worth mentioning that Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules, 1955 has been declared ultra-virus by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
However, no evidence has been lead by the accused persons that the sampled commodity was not misbranded.
No date of packaging has been provided and no Best before date has been provided on the label.
In fact, even the name of the commodity and the ingredients, the name of manufacturer and complete address have not been provided in the label.
Also, it has been proved that the label was also not of the standard size as required mandate as per Rule 36 of the PFA Rules by the complainant which is an violation of PFA Rules.

18. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid facts and discussions, Accused persons namely Kishan Dutt Sharma and M/s. Bengali Sweet House are convicted for the violation of provisions of Section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act, 1954 along with violation of Rule 32 and 36 of PFA Rules, 1955 punishable u/s 16(1)(a) r/w Section 7 of PFA Act,1954.
19.
Let the matter be listed for arguments on sentence.
